source: built-in example; MoM and REML, default axes
plain: The analysis combined 13 effect estimates from 6 studies, allowing effects from the same study to be related. The recommended REML average was 0.296 (95% confidence interval 0.183 to 0.410) on the supplied effect scale. If zero represents no effect on that scale, there is evidence of a difference (the confidence interval excludes no effect). The meaning and clinical importance of the effect depend on the measure supplied; this analysis alone does not establish causation. With few independent studies, treat these results as descriptive.
methods: The page fits an intercept-only three-level model to the supplied effects and squared standard errors, without transformation or back-transformation. The recommended fit uses restricted maximum likelihood (REML), with a study random intercept and an independent effect random intercept nested within study, diagonal sampling-error covariance, and generalized least squares pooling. Its 95% normal Wald CI uses the model-based SE. No p-value is computed or reported. The separate method-of-moments (MoM) fit starts from inverse-variance study means and DerSimonian–Laird moments, then iterates between-study and within-study moment updates with nonnegative variance components. Final MoM weights are the inverse of sampling variance plus both heterogeneity components. The page displays a normal Wald CI and a residual-scale HKSJ-labelled t CI: the weighted squared residual sum is divided by the cluster degrees of freedom, floored at one, and used to inflate the pooled variance. The t degrees of freedom are the number of studies minus one, with a minimum of one. This is not cluster-robust inference. The MoM prediction interval is the pooled effect ± t × √(between-study variance + within-study variance + adjusted SE squared), using cluster degrees of freedom; it is available from two studies. No REML prediction interval is computed. MoM variance shares divide each heterogeneity component and the typical sampling variance by their sum; typical sampling variance is (number of effects minus one) × sum of inverse sampling variances, divided by the squared sum minus the sum of squared inverse sampling variances. Study forest intervals and the MoM pooled diamond use normal Wald limits. The R forest instead shows REML pooling, so their diamonds need not coincide. Analyses were run in allmeta multilevel-ma <build.version> (commit <build.shortSha>).
results: There were 13 effects in 6 studies. REML pooled effect = 0.296, SE = 0.058, 95% CI 0.183 to 0.410; between-study variance = 0.0137; within-study variance = 0.0000; restricted log-likelihood = 8.432. MoM pooled effect = 0.313, SE = 0.046, 95% normal CI 0.223 to 0.404; adjusted t CI 0.166 to 0.461 with 5 cluster degrees of freedom. MoM 95% prediction interval = −0.016 to 0.642. MoM between-study variance = 0.0131 (share 48.8%); within-study variance = 0.0000 (share 0.0%); sampling-variance share = 51.2%; shares total 100.0%.
flags: Small-cluster inference is descriptive; the adjusted MoM interval is not cluster-robust. Small-study-effect tests would be underpowered and were not performed.
The R comparison verifies REML only. MoM results, variance shares and prediction limits are not verified by that comparison.
